That which is revealed unto t .. 43 They who disbelieve say: Thou art no messenger (of Allah). Say: Allah, and whosoever hath knowledge of the Scripture, is sufficient witness between me and you.

l: prayer, Surah 13: The Thunder (Ar-Ra'd), Surah 13: The Thunder (Ar-Ra'd) / 1 Alif. Lam. Mim. Ra. These are verses of the Scripture. That which is revealed unto t .. 43 They who disbelieve say: Thou art no messenger (of Allah). Say: Allah, and whosoever hath knowledge of the Scripture, is sufficient witness between me and you.

That which is revealed unto t .. 43 They who disbelieve say: Thou art no messenger (of Allah). Say: Allah, and whosoever hath knowledge of the Scripture, is sufficient witness between me and you.

l: Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The unit concerns Allah’s revelation of Scripture through a messenger to bring mankind from darkness to light and guide them to the way of Allah. It recounts Moses’ call to his people, the rejection of messengers by earlier peoples, the fate of disbelievers in Hell, and the reward of believers in the Gardens. It presents Allah’s signs in the heavens and the earth, Abraham’s prayers concerning worship, his descendants, and the holy House, and warnings about the Day of Judgment. It concludes that the clear message teaches that Allah is One and calls people of understanding to take heed.

l: Allah, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: Allah reveals Scripture, guides and sends astray whom He will, and is the Creator and Owner of what is in the heavens and the earth. He promises increase to those who give thanks, destroys wrong-doers, rewards believers, and will repay every soul for what it has earned.

l: Scripture, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: Scripture is revealed to a messenger so that mankind may be brought from darkness to light, by the permission of Allah, unto the path of the Mighty, the Owner of Praise.

l: mankind, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: Mankind is called to leave darkness for light, heed the warnings, worship Allah, and reflect on His signs. Mankind is also warned of the day when the doom will come and wrong-doers will seek reprieve.

l: the believers, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The believers are told to put their trust in Allah, establish worship, and spend from what they have been given. Those who believe and do good works enter Gardens where they abide by permission of Allah.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The disbelievers prefer the life of the world to the Hereafter, debar others from the way of Allah, and are described as far astray. Their works are likened to ashes blown away by the wind, and they face Hell and a painful doom.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The Hereafter is preferred over the life of the world by those who follow the way of Allah. Allah confirms believers in the Hereafter and warns that the disbelievers face punishment there.

l: the way of Allah, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The way of Allah is the path to which Scripture brings mankind. The disbelievers debar people from it and would have it crooked.

l: the heavens, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The heavens belong to Allah, who created them with truth and can remove mankind and bring forth a new creation. On the final day, the heavens will be changed and people will come forth unto Allah.

l: the earth, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The earth belongs to Allah, who created it with truth and provides its water and fruits. On the final day, the earth will be changed to other than the earth.

l: an awful doom, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: An awful doom awaits the disbelievers who reject Allah and turn people away from His way.

l: a messenger, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: A messenger is sent with the language of his folk so that the message may be made clear to them. Messengers call people to Allah, but some people reject them and demand a clear warrant.

l: Moses, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: Moses is sent with Allah’s revelations to bring his people from darkness to light and remind them of the days of Allah. He reminds them of Allah’s favor in delivering them from Pharaoh’s folk and calls them to trust and give thanks.

l: Hell, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: Hell is before the froward potentate and contains festering water that is difficult to swallow. The guilty are exposed to it, and those who exchanged Allah’s grace for thanklessness are led to it.

l: Satan, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: Satan says that Allah promised a true promise while he promised and failed. He admits that he had no power except to call people, that they obeyed him, and that they must blame themselves.

l: the Gardens, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The Gardens are entered by those who believe and do good works. Rivers flow beneath them, they abide there by permission of Allah, and their greeting is Peace.

l: a goodly saying, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: A goodly saying is likened to a goodly tree whose root is firm and whose branches reach into heaven. It gives its fruit at every season by permission of its Lord.

l: a goodly tree, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: A goodly tree has a firm root, branches reaching into heaven, and fruit at every season by permission of its Lord.

l: worship, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: Worship is to be established by believers and is the purpose Abraham seeks for himself and some of his posterity. Abraham asks Allah to preserve him and his sons from serving idols.

l: the heavens and the earth, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The heavens and the earth are created by Allah with truth, and Allah causes water to descend and produces fruits for mankind. He also makes the ships, rivers, sun, moon, night, and day serviceable to mankind.

l: Abraham, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: Abraham asks Allah to make his territory safe, preserve him and his sons from serving idols, and incline hearts toward his posterity. He asks for provision for them, the establishment of worship, forgiveness, and acceptance of his prayer.

l: the holy House, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The holy House is near the uncultivable valley where Abraham settles some of his posterity so that they may establish proper worship.

l: the uncultivable valley, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The uncultivable valley is near the holy House, where Abraham settles some of his posterity. He asks Allah to provide its people with fruits so that they may be thankful.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: The Day of Judgment is a day when the guilty will come forth in chains, their raiment of pitch and the Fire covering their faces. Wrong-doers will ask for reprieve, but Allah will repay each soul for what it has earned.

l: a clear message, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: A clear message is given for mankind so that they may be warned, know that Allah is only One Allah, and take heed as people of understanding.

l: revelation, Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim), Surah 14: Abraham (Ibrahim)
s: Revelation is given to Moses and is sent through messengers to make Allah’s message clear to their peoples. It brings mankind from darkness to light by the permission of Allah.

l: Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: This unit concerns Allah’s signs, commandments, mercy, and punishments, including the Night Journey of His servant from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far distant place of worship. It recounts what happened to Moses, the Children of Israel, Iblis, and mankind, and describes guidance, worship, resurrection, the Hereafter, reward, and hell. It teaches believers to worship Allah alone, honor parents, protect life and wealth, keep covenants, avoid adultery and wrongdoing, and speak kindly. It presents the Qur'an as guidance, healing, and mercy, and declares that Truth has come while falsehood is bound to vanish.

l: Allah, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Allah carries His servant by night, reveals the Qur'an, guides whom He wills, provides for mankind, and knows and sees His slaves. He commands worship of Him alone, shows mercy, and appoints reward and punishment.

l: Muhammad, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Muhammad is carried by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far distant place of worship. He is instructed to recite the Qur'an, convey warning and good tidings, speak kindly, establish worship, and call people to Allah.

l: Moses, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Moses is given the Scripture as guidance for the Children of Israel and receives nine clear tokens. Pharaoh calls him bewitched, but Moses declares that the tokens were sent by the Lord of the heavens and the earth.

l: Iblis, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Iblis refuses to prostrate before Adam because Adam was created from clay. He asks for respite until the Day of Resurrection and vows to seize most of Adam’s seed, but Allah says he has no power over faithful bondmen.

l: Children of Israel, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: The Children of Israel are given guidance and warned that they will work corruption in the earth twice. They receive power, wealth, and children, but punishment comes when they repeat corruption.

l: mankind, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Mankind is honored, carried on land and sea, and provided with good things. Mankind is also described as hasty, thankless, grudging, and prone to disbelief, while each person is accountable for his own conduct.

l: believers, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Believers who do good works are promised a great reward. The Qur'an is described as healing and mercy for them.

l: disbelievers, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Disbelievers reject the Qur'an, demand signs, and deny resurrection. Hell is appointed as their dungeon and painful doom.

l: devil, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: The devil sows discord among people, is an open foe to mankind, and promises only to deceive. He is associated with squanderers, who are called his brothers.

l: Inviolable Place of Worship, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: The Inviolable Place of Worship is the starting place from which Allah carries His servant by night.

l: Far distant place of worship, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: The Far distant place of worship is the destination of the Night Journey, and its neighbourhood is described as blessed.

l: earth, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: The earth is described as praising Allah together with the heavens and all things in it. Mankind is warned that it cannot rend the earth or reach the height of the hills.

l: heaven, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: The heaven is among Allah’s creation and praises Him with the earth and all things therein. The disbelievers demand that heaven fall upon them or that Muhammad ascend into it.

l: hell, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Hell is appointed as a dungeon for disbelievers and as the payment of those who follow Iblis. Its flame is increased whenever it abates for those who disbelieve Allah’s revelations.

l: Qur'an, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: The Qur'an guides to what is straightest and gives good tidings to believers who do good works. It is a healing and mercy for believers, a warning to wrongdoers, and cannot be matched by mankind and the jinn.

l: Hereafter, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: The Hereafter is the future state in which people are resurrected, summoned with their records, and judged. It is greater in degrees and preferment than the hastening life of this world.

l: Night Journey, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: The Night Journey concerns Allah’s carrying His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far distant place of worship so that He may show him of His tokens.

l: revelation, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Revelation is sent by Allah to Muhammad and is divided for recitation to mankind at intervals. Allah states that what He reveals is by His mercy and that He can withdraw it if He wills.

l: resurrection, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Resurrection is described as the raising of people after they become bones and fragments. On the Day of Resurrection, people are summoned with their records and given their books in their right or other hands.

l: worship, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Worship is to be established from the going down of the sun until the dark of night, with Qur'an recited at dawn. People are commanded to worship none save Allah and to call upon Him with His beautiful names.

l: guidance, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Guidance is provided by the Scripture and the Qur'an, which guides to the straightest way. Whoever follows guidance does so for the good of his own soul.

l: mercy, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Allah’s mercy is hoped for by those who seek nearness to Him and is shown in His provision and revelation. People are instructed to ask for mercy for their parents.

l: punishment, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Punishment comes upon those who corrupt, disbelieve, follow Iblis, or reject Allah’s revelations. Allah threatens repeated punishment if wrongdoing is repeated and describes punishment in hell.

l: sin, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: The unit forbids killing children, adultery, wrongful killing, misuse of orphan wealth, dishonest measuring, following what one does not know, and exultant walking. It calls the killing of children a great sin.

l: wealth, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Wealth is to be given in due measure to kinsmen, the needy, and the wayfarer, without wanton squandering. The wealth of an orphan must not be approached except in the better manner until the orphan reaches strength.

l: Truth, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Truth has come and is declared to have prevailed. The Qur'an is sent down with truth and descended with truth.

l: falsehood, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: Falsehood has vanished away and is bound to vanish. Those who follow it are described as astray and unable to find a road.

l: reward, Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa), Surah 17: The Night Journey (Al-Israa)
s: A great reward is promised to believers who do good works. Those who desire the Hereafter and strive for it as believers have efforts that find favor with their Lord.

l: Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: This unit praises Allah for revealing the Scripture to Muhammad and warns believers and disbelievers about judgment, reward, and punishment. It recounts the People of the Cave, the two men and their gardens, and the meeting of Moses with the knowledgeable servant. It also tells of Dhu'l-Qarneyn, the people between the two mountains, and the barrier built against Gog and Magog. The unit emphasizes Allah's power, guidance, mercy, promise, and the limits of worldly life.

l: Allah, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Allah revealed the Scripture to His slave, guides whom He wills, and alone has true protection, judgment, power, and worship. He rewards believers, punishes wrongdoing and disbelief, shows mercy, and knows the unseen, including the duration of the People of the Cave's stay.

l: Muhammad, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Muhammad is addressed as the recipient of the revealed Scripture and is told to warn, recite, restrain himself with those who remember Allah, and proclaim that Allah is One.

l: the Scripture, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The Scripture was revealed by Allah to His slave. It contains warnings, promises, accounts, similitudes, and guidance, and none can change Allah's words.

l: the believers, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The believers do good works and receive the news of a fair reward, enduring gardens, and Paradise. They are encouraged to remain with those who call upon Allah and seek His Countenance.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The disbelievers reject Allah's revelations, dispute the truth, mock the revelations and messengers, and face hell, punishment, and loss of the value of their works.

l: the People of the Cave, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The People of the Cave were young men who believed in their Lord and sought refuge in the Cave. Allah sealed their hearing, preserved them for years, awakened them, and disclosed them as a sign that His promise and the Hour are true.

l: the Cave, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The Cave sheltered the young believers, while Allah caused the sun to move away from them and caused them to turn over while asleep. They remained there for three hundred years and add nine.

l: the Hour, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The Hour is certain and there is no doubt concerning it. The unit warns that people may deny it and teaches that Allah will gather creation for it.

l: Paradise, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Paradise is described as the Gardens of Paradise prepared as a welcome for those who believe and do good works. They will abide there without wishing to leave.

l: hell, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Hell is prepared for disbelievers and is presented plainly to them. Its punishment includes fire, molten-like water, and a calamitous resting-place.

l: the life of the world, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The life of the world is compared to vegetation made dry and scattered by the wind. Its wealth and children are an ornament, while enduring good deeds are better with Allah.

l: the two gardens, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The two gardens belonged to one of the two men and contained grapes, date-palms, tillage, abundant fruit, and a river. They were destroyed after their owner was warned, leaving him regretful.

l: the two men, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The two men are presented in a similitude about wealth, gardens, belief, and pride. One boasted of greater wealth and doubted the Hour, while the other rebuked him and affirmed Allah's oneness.

l: the garden owner's comrade, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The garden owner's comrade reminded him that Allah created him from dust, a drop, and then as a man. He urged him to acknowledge Allah's power and later witnessed the destruction of the garden.

l: Moses, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Moses traveled with his servant seeking the meeting point of the two rivers and later followed the knowledgeable servant to learn. He repeatedly questioned actions he could not understand and was told that he could not bear with them patiently.

l: Moses's servant, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Moses's servant accompanied him on the journey and forgot the fish at the rock, attributing the forgetfulness to Satan. He later informed Moses that the fish had taken its way into the waters.

l: the knowledgeable servant, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The knowledgeable servant had received mercy and knowledge from Allah. He damaged a ship, slew a lad, and repaired a wall, then explained that each act served a hidden purpose ordained by Allah.

l: the ship, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The ship belonged to poor people working on the river. The knowledgeable servant damaged it because a king behind them was taking every ship by force.

l: the king, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The king behind the poor people was taking every ship by force. His threat was the reason the ship was damaged.

l: the lad, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The lad was slain by the knowledgeable servant because his future rebellion and disbelief were feared for his believing parents. Allah intended to replace him with one better in purity and nearer to mercy.

l: the two orphan boys, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The two orphan boys owned the wall and the treasure beneath it. Their righteous father and Allah's mercy protected the treasure until they reached full strength.

l: the wall, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The wall belonged to the two orphan boys and was near collapse. The knowledgeable servant repaired it without taking payment so that the treasure beneath it would remain protected.

l: Dhu'l-Qarneyn, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Dhu'l-Qarneyn was made strong in the land and given a road to every thing. He traveled to the setting-place and rising-place of the sun and then to the region between the two mountains, acting with justice and building a barrier against Gog and Magog.

l: Gog and Magog, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Gog and Magog were spoiling the land and could not surmount or pierce the barrier built against them. The barrier will be laid low when Allah's promise comes to pass.

l: the people between the two mountains, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The people between the two mountains could scarcely understand speech and asked Dhu'l-Qarneyn to build a barrier against Gog and Magog. He accepted their assistance with strength instead of their tribute.

l: the two mountains, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The two mountains marked the place where Dhu'l-Qarneyn found the people threatened by Gog and Magog. He leveled the gap between them with iron and molten copper to form the barrier.

l: the barrier, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The barrier was built from pieces of iron and molten copper between the two mountains. Gog and Magog could neither climb over it nor pierce it, but it will be laid low when Allah's promise arrives.

l: Iblis, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Iblis was of the jinn and rebelled against Allah's command when he refused to fall prostrate before Adam. He and his seed are presented as enemies who should not be chosen as protecting friends.

l: the angels, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The angels were commanded to fall prostrate before Adam, and they did so except for Iblis.

l: Adam, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Adam was the one before whom the angels were commanded to fall prostrate. His creation is referenced as part of the account of Iblis's rebellion.

l: the partners of Allah, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The partners of Allah are false objects of worship that cannot hear prayers or help their claimants. Those who invoke them will find a gulf of doom between themselves and their supposed partners.

l: the messengers, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The messengers were sent as bearers of good news and warners. Disbelievers disputed with falsehood and mocked the revelations and what the messengers warned them about.

l: the revelations of Allah, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The revelations of Allah provide guidance, warnings, similitudes, and reminders. Some people turn away from them, forget what they have sent forward, or treat them as a jest.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: On the Day of Resurrection, people will be gathered, their deeds will confront them, and the works of disbelievers will receive no weight. The believers who do good works will receive Paradise.

l: the Judgment, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The Judgment includes the placing of the Book, the exposure of every deed, and the punishment or reward of people. Allah does not wrong anyone.

l: the Words of Allah, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The Words of Allah cannot be changed. Even if the sea became ink, it would be exhausted before the Words of Allah were exhausted.

l: guidance, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Guidance comes from Allah, and the one whom Allah guides is rightly led. People who turn away from the revelations or follow their own lust may not be led aright.

l: mercy, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: Allah's mercy is sought by the young men of the Cave and is given to the knowledgeable servant. It is also shown in the protection of the orphan boys' treasure and in Allah's patience toward wrongdoers.

l: the promise of Allah, Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf), Surah 18: The Cave (Al-Kahf) / 1 Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed
s: The promise of Allah is true, including the promise of the Hour and the final events involving the barrier. The People of the Cave were disclosed so that people would know that the promise is true.

l: Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: This unit concerns Allah's mercy, commands, and judgments, especially as shown through Zachariah, John, Mary, Jesus, Abraham, Moses, Ishmael, and Idris. It recounts the births, missions, worship, and conduct of John and Jesus, and describes the guidance and trials of earlier prophets. It warns the disbelievers of resurrection, punishment, hell, and the Day of anguish, while promising the believers and righteous the Garden and Allah's love. It affirms that Allah has no son, that all beings belong to Him, and that all will return to Him.

l: Allah, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them. He creates, guides, shows mercy, commands worship, raises the dead, gathers people for judgment, rewards the righteous, and punishes the disbelievers.

l: Zachariah, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: Zachariah secretly cries to Allah, asking for a successor because his wife is barren and he fears for his kinsfolk after him. Allah gives him the tidings of John and makes his sign that he will not speak to mankind for three nights despite having no bodily defect.

l: John, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: John is given his name, wisdom as a child, compassion, purity, and devotion. He is dutiful toward his parents and is described as neither arrogant nor rebellious.

l: Mary, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: Mary withdraws from her people to a chamber and receives the Spirit in the likeness of a perfect man. She conceives Jesus, gives birth in hardship, and returns to her people carrying him.

l: Abraham, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: Abraham is described as a saint and a prophet. He urges his father to abandon powerless gods and serve Allah, withdraws from his people and their worship, and is then given Isaac and Jacob.

l: Muhammad, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: Muhammad is addressed as the one who warns people of the Day of anguish and other promised events. His tongue is made suitable for the Scripture so that he may give good tidings to those who ward off evil and warn the froward.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: The disbelievers reject Allah's revelations, dispute the believers' position, and claim that the Beneficent has taken a son. They face punishment, hell, confusion by devils, and the gathering before Allah.

l: the believers, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: The believers are contrasted with those who disbelieve and are associated with better guidance and lasting good works. Those who believe and do good works receive love from the Beneficent.

l: the righteous, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: The righteous are gathered as a goodly company unto the Beneficent. They are rescued from hell and inherit the Garden.

l: the heavens, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: The heavens are nearly torn apart by the claim that the Beneficent has taken a son. They belong to Allah and all come unto Him as slaves.

l: the earth, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: The earth is described as nearly split asunder by the claim that the Beneficent has taken a son. Allah inherits it and all who are upon it.

l: hell, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: Hell is where the guilty are driven and where the stubbornly rebellious are identified as most worthy to be burned. The evil-doers remain crouching there, while those who kept from evil are rescued.

l: the Garden, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: The Garden is promised by the Beneficent to His slaves in the unseen. Its people hear no idle talk, receive peace and food morning and evening, and it is inherited by the devout.

l: the Scripture, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: The Scripture recounts the accounts of prophets and commands remembrance of them. It is made easy in Muhammad's tongue so that he may give good tidings and warnings.

l: the revelations, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: The revelations of the Beneficent cause the prophets' descendants and chosen servants to fall down adoring and weeping. The disbelievers reject the clear revelations.

l: worship, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: Worship includes prayer, almsgiving, service to Allah, and steadfastness in His service. Later generations ruin worship and follow lusts, while the prophets and righteous uphold it.

l: mercy, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: Allah's mercy is shown to Zachariah, Mary, Jesus, Abraham, and other prophets and servants. The Garden is promised through the mercy of the Beneficent, and Jesus is described as a mercy from Allah for mankind.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: On the Day of Resurrection, each person comes to Allah alone. The righteous are gathered to the Beneficent, while the guilty are driven to hell.

l: the Day of anguish, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: The Day of anguish is the day when the case has been decided. People are warned because they are presently careless and do not believe.

l: the Hour, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: The Hour is among the events promised to those in error. When they behold it or its punishment, they will know who is worse in position and weaker as an army.

l: the Judgment, Surah 19: Mary (Maryam), Surah 19: Mary (Maryam)
s: The text describes a day when the case is decided, people are gathered before Allah, and each one comes to Him alone. The righteous are rewarded and the guilty are punished.

l: Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: This unit concerns the revelation of the Qur'an to Muhammad and Allah's commands, guidance, and warnings. It recounts Moses' mission to Pharaoh, the signs given to Moses, the contest with Pharaoh's magicians, and the deliverance of the Children of Israel through the sea. It describes the Children of Israel's trial with As-Samiri and the calf, and Moses' response. It also presents teachings about Adam, Iblis, the Garden, guidance, resurrection, the Day of Judgment, hell, and the Hereafter.

l: Qur'an, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: The Qur'an is revealed as a reminder, in Arabic, containing threats and lessons so that people may avoid evil and take heed. Muhammad is told not to hasten with it before its revelation is perfected.

l: Muhammad, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Muhammad receives the Qur'an and is told to bear patiently with what people say, praise Allah, and ask for increased knowledge.

l: Allah, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Allah is described as the only deity, the Creator, the Beneficent, the True King, and the One who knows what is hidden and apparent. Allah guides, forgives, provides, judges, and rewards or punishes people according to their deeds.

l: the Hour, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: The Hour is surely coming, but Allah keeps its time hidden so that every soul may be rewarded for what it strives to achieve.

l: Moses, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Moses is chosen, addressed by Allah, given signs, and sent with Aaron to Pharaoh. He asks for ease, eloquence, and Aaron's help, confronts Pharaoh's magicians, leads the Children of Israel away by night, and returns angrily when they worship the calf.

l: Moses' staff, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Moses' staff is used for leaning, tending sheep, and other purposes. When he casts it down, it becomes a serpent, and Allah commands him to take it without fear.

l: Pharaoh, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Pharaoh is described as having transgressed and as leading his people astray. He challenges Moses, threatens Moses' followers and the magicians, pursues the Children of Israel, and is covered by the sea with his hosts.

l: Aaron, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Aaron is appointed to share Moses' task and strengthen him. He warns the Children of Israel against the calf, but they refuse to stop worshipping it until Moses returns.

l: Children of Israel, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: The Children of Israel are delivered from Pharaoh, given a covenant, and provided manna and quails. In Moses' absence, many are misled by As-Samiri into worshipping the calf.

l: Pharaoh's magicians, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Pharaoh's magicians make their cords and staves appear to run by their magic. They accept defeat, believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses, and refuse to prefer Pharaoh over the clear proofs.

l: magic, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Magic makes the cords and staves appear to move, but Moses' sign consumes what the magicians have made. The magicians confess that Allah is better and more lasting, and Pharaoh threatens them for believing.

l: As-Samiri, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: As-Samiri misleads the Children of Israel during Moses' absence and produces the calf from the ornaments. Moses condemns him and declares that he will have a tryst he cannot break.

l: the calf, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: The calf is made of a saffron hue and gives forth a lowing sound. The Children of Israel call it their god, but it cannot return a saying or possess harm or benefit; Moses burns it and scatters its dust over the sea.

l: sea, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Allah commands Moses to make a dry path through the sea for the Children of Israel. Pharaoh follows with his hosts, and the sea covers them.

l: hell, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Hell is the destination of whoever comes to his Lord guilty. There the guilty person neither dies nor lives.

l: Gardens of Eden, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow, are prepared for believers who do good works. They remain there forever as the reward of those who grow.

l: resurrection, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: The text describes people being brought forth again and assembled after the Trumpet is blown. The guilty are gathered in terror, and the mountains are reduced to scattered dust.

l: Adam, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Adam receives a covenant but forgets and lacks constancy. He eats from the forbidden tree, then is chosen, forgiven, and guided by his Lord.

l: Iblis, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Iblis refuses Allah's command to prostrate before Adam. He is identified as an enemy of Adam and his wife.

l: the angels, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: The angels are commanded to prostrate before Adam, and all do so except Iblis.

l: the Garden, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: The Garden is a place where Adam and his wife do not hunger, become naked, thirst, or suffer the sun's heat. They are sent down from it after eating from the tree.

l: the devil, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: The devil whispers to Adam and presents the tree of immortality and power that does not waste away. His whisper leads Adam and his wife to eat from the tree and become aware of their shame.

l: guidance, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Allah promises that whoever follows His guidance will not go astray or come to grief. Guidance is connected with following revelation and walking aright.

l: worship, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Moses is commanded to serve Allah and establish worship for His remembrance. Muhammad is told to enjoin worship upon his people and remain constant in it.

l: remembrance of Allah, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Allah commands Moses and Aaron not to be faint in His remembrance. Muhammad is told to glorify Allah at various times, and turning away from remembrance is linked to a narrow life.

l: faith, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Faith is shown by the magicians who believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses and by those who come to Allah as believers. Believers who do good works receive high stations and fear no injustice.

l: good works, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Good works accompany belief and lead to high stations and the Gardens of Eden. Allah does not diminish the reward of those who do good works.

l: punishment, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Punishment is threatened for those who lie against Allah, deny revelation, turn away, or come to their Lord guilty. Pharaoh threatens punishment, while Allah's punishment includes hell and the burden borne on the Day of Resurrection.

l: revelation, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: Revelation comes from Allah and includes the Qur'an, the commands given to Moses, and the guidance sent to people. It is presented as a reminder, warning, and proof.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: The Hereafter is described as more severe and lasting for those who reject Allah's revelations. It includes reward in the Gardens of Eden and punishment in hell.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 20: Taa-Haa, Surah 20: Taa-Haa
s: On the Day of Judgment, the Trumpet is blown, the guilty are assembled, intercession benefits only by Allah's permission, and faces humble themselves before the Living, the Eternal. Those who turn away from remembrance are brought blind and face the consequences of their deeds.

l: Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Surah 21 concerns the approaching reckoning of mankind, the oneness of Allah, and the rejection of idolatry. It recounts how Allah supported messengers and prophets including Abraham, Lot, Moses, Aaron, Noah, David, Solomon, Job, Dhu'n-Nun, and Zachariah, while destroying wrong-doing peoples. It describes revelation, resurrection, the balance of justice, punishment in hell, and mercy for the righteous and believers. Muhammad is sent as a mercy for the peoples and warns that Allah is One.

l: Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: It presents warnings about the approaching reckoning, the oneness of Allah, the fate of wrong-doers, and the mercy shown to believers and the righteous.

l: Allah, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Allah is the One Lord, Creator and Sustainer of the heavens and the earth. He sends revelation, supports His messengers, judges justly, punishes wrong-doers, and shows mercy to the righteous.

l: Muhammad, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Muhammad is warned that mankind's reckoning is near and is mocked by those who disbelieve. He is sent as a mercy for the peoples and instructed to proclaim that Allah is One.

l: mankind, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Mankind's reckoning draws near while many turn away heedlessly. Mankind is made of haste and every soul must taste death.

l: the wrong-doers, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The wrong-doers reject the message, mock messengers, and ask for portents. They are threatened with punishment and destruction.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The disbelievers deny revelation, mock Muhammad, and question the promised punishment. They will face fire that comes upon them unexpectedly.

l: the messengers, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The messengers before Muhammad were men who received inspiration. They were mocked, but what their mockers ridiculed eventually surrounded the mockers.

l: the prophets, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The prophets received inspiration and guided people by Allah's command. They established worship, performed good deeds, and gave alms.

l: the angels, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The angels worship Allah without pride or weariness and glorify Him night and day. They will welcome the righteous on the promised Day.

l: the idolaters, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The idolaters choose gods beside Allah and worship what cannot benefit or harm them. They and what they worship are described as fuel for hell.

l: the believers, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The believers are saved from anguish and benefit from Allah's mercy. Their good works are recorded and not rejected.

l: the righteous, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The righteous are guided, brought into Allah's mercy, and promised inheritance of the earth. They will be far removed from hell and protected from its sound.

l: the peoples, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Muhammad is sent as a mercy for the peoples. The peoples are warned to surrender to the One Allah.

l: Abraham, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Abraham rejects the worship of images and breaks the idols, leaving their chief intact so his people may question it. Allah makes the fire coolness and peace for him and rescues him with Lot.

l: Lot, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Lot is rescued from a community that practiced abominations. He is brought into Allah's mercy and counted among the righteous.

l: Moses, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Moses is given the Criterion, a light, and a Reminder for those who keep from evil.

l: Aaron, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Aaron is given the Criterion together with Moses as a light and a Reminder for those who keep from evil.

l: Noah, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Noah cries to his Lord, and Allah hears his prayer, saves him and his household from the great affliction, and delivers him from those who denied the revelations.

l: David, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: David gives judgment concerning a field damaged by people's sheep. Allah gives him judgment and knowledge and causes the hills and birds to hymn praise with him.

l: Solomon, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Solomon is given understanding in the judgment concerning the field. The wind and certain evil ones are subdued to him by Allah's command.

l: Job, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Job cries to his Lord about adversity. Allah hears his prayer, removes his affliction, and restores his household and the like thereof as a mercy.

l: Dhu'n-Nun, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Dhu'n-Nun cries from the darkness, confessing that there is no Allah save Allah and that he has been a wrong-doer. Allah hears his prayer and saves him from anguish.

l: Zachariah, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Zachariah asks Allah not to leave him childless. Allah hears his prayer, bestows John upon him, and adjusts his wife to bear a child.

l: Mary, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: She who was chaste is made, together with her son, a token for all peoples after Allah breathes into her something of His Spirit.

l: the son of Mary, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The son of the chaste woman is made a token for all peoples.

l: the heavens, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The heavens and the earth were once of one piece before Allah parted them. The heavens belong to Allah, and He will roll them up as a recorder rolls up a written scroll.

l: the earth, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Allah places firm hills and ravines in the earth and makes it a place where people may find their way. The earth belongs to Him, and the righteous will inherit it.

l: the land which We had blessed, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Abraham and Lot are brought to the land which We had blessed for all peoples. The wind is directed toward it by Solomon's command.

l: the Scripture, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The Scripture is revealed as a Reminder for mankind. It contains the promise that Allah's righteous slaves will inherit the earth.

l: the Reminder, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The Reminder comes from Allah and is rejected by many who turn away. Moses and Aaron are given a Reminder, and the revealed Scripture is described as a blessed Reminder.

l: the Criterion, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The Criterion is given to Moses and Aaron as a means of distinguishing right from wrong, together with a light and a Reminder.

l: the revelations, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The revelations are denied by evil peoples, for which they are destroyed. Muhammad warns mankind through inspiration.

l: the inspiration, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Inspiration is given to the messengers and tells them that there is no Allah save One Allah. Muhammad is warned and instructed through it.

l: the idols, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The idols are images worshipped by Abraham's father and people. Abraham breaks them into fragments except for their chief.

l: the fire, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The fire is commanded to be coolness and peace for Abraham. The disbelievers will be unable to repel the fire of punishment.

l: Gog and Magog, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Gog and Magog will be let loose and hasten out of every mound before the True Promise draws near.

l: hell, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Hell is the destination of the idolaters and what they worship beside Allah. Wailing is their portion there, and they will abide in it.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: On the Day of Resurrection Allah sets a just balance so that no soul is wronged, even by the weight of a mustard seed.

l: the Hour, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The Hour is feared by those who dread doom. The devout are described as those who fear their Lord and dread the Hour.

l: the True Promise, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa), Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The True Promise draws near when Gog and Magog are released and the disbelievers stare in terror.
